contrary_evidence: WHO TrACSS 2026 reports 173 of 183 countries with plans; only 22% report funding plus full implementation and 36% report reference-laboratory capacity.
WOAH ANIMUSE 2024 covers 74% of estimated global food-animal biomass with 119 participants; reported quantities and coverage-adjusted estimates are distinguished.
Only five of 119 quantitative ANIMUSE participants used farm records as a validated quantitative source.
The 80-participant ANIMUSE 2019–2024 cohort shows a 3% decline; a separate 74-participant 2018–2024 analysis is cited as showing a 9% increase, with provenance qualified.
ECDC 2025 reports at least 50% third-generation cephalosporin resistance in K. pneumoniae in 21 of 43 reporting countries and at least 50% carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter spp. in 21 of 38.
EU carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae bloodstream-infection incidence is 3.75 per 100,000 in 2025, 72% above 2019 and 1.68 above the EU 2030 target of 2.07.
The 2024 UN political declaration commits to meaningfully reducing antimicrobial quantities used globally in agrifood systems by 2030.
limitations: TrACSS is a country self-assessment, not an independent audit of budget execution or service quality.
ANIMUSE quantities are primarily derived from sales/import records; only five of 119 quantitative participants used farm records.
ANIMUSE trend cohorts and observation periods differ.
ECDC country-threshold results concern invasive clinical isolates, not community prevalence.
EU-level ESAC-Net targets and indicators remain distinct from the EU/EEA community-consumption series.
Available datasets do not establish a causal link between animal antimicrobial use and the human resistance patterns presented.
